## keyfile.hex Format Documentation {#keyfile.hex-format-documentation .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

1\. Purpose

The \`keyfile.hex\` format serves two primary objectives for RC40 devices:

- Initial Provisioning: Critical cryptographic material like root certificate, decryption key and passwords are securely injected during the production phase.

- Field Updates: Critical cryptographic material like root certificate, decryption key and passwords are securely updated on RC40 already deployed in the field.

2\. General Specifications

- Endianness: All integer fields within the \`keyfile.hex\` are encoded in Big-Endian format (Most Significant Byte first), irrespective of the target architecture.

- Deployment: \`keyfile.hex\` files are flashed onto RC40 with CB-ME version (or higher) using BODAS-service flashing tool.

- Keyfile Update and Protection Mechanisms:

  To ensure the integrity, authenticity, and secure deployment of \`keyfile.hex\` updates, the following mechanisms are implemented:

oUpdate Verification Protocol

§Before any changes are applied to the RC\'s cryptographic storage, the following steps are mandatory:

- Buffering and Verification: The entire \`keyfile.hex\` content is buffered into RAM by RC40. A comprehensive verification process (e.g., integrity check) is successfully completed before any data is written to persistent storage.

- Downgrade Protection: A dedicated counter tracks the version of the active \`keyfile.hex\`. Any incoming \`keyfile.hex\` with a version number equal to or lower than the currently active version will be rejected to prevent the re-introduction of older, potentially vulnerable security settings.

oAccess Control and Authentication

§Strict access controls are enforced to authorize \`keyfile.hex\` updates:

- Authentication Requirement: Users must authenticate with a Level 1 flashing password before initiating a \`keyfile.hex\` update. This ensures that only authorized personnel can modify the device\'s security configuration.

oPassword Provisioning Rules

§The provisioning and updating of access level passwords via keyfile are subject to specific security constraints:

- One-time operation : This mechanism is enabled, if the ECU lacks security functions(i.e.neither a signature nor a decryption setting is present), and any one(or more) of the 10 available access level passwords is changed for the first time using any of the following methods

                    1:via UDS service 0xBE: [Security change password in CB-ME](security-change-password-in-cb.html "Security-Change-Password-in-CB"){.topiclink}.

                2:via C-API: [bds_sec_saveSecret](bds_sec_savesecret.html "bds_sec_saveSecret"){.topiclink}.

                          3:via keyfile: An unsecured keyfile write(i.e.neither a signature nor a decryption setting is present on same keyfile).

- Once one-time operation has been enabled, the ability to set passwords via keyfile will be permanently disabled.

oUse cases:

1.Keyfile contains signature info + access level passwords: Updates signature info, skips access level password updates.

2.Keyfile contains decryption key + access level passwords: Updates decryption key, skips access level password updates.

3.Keyfile contains signature info + decryption key + access level passwords: Updates signature info and decryption key, skips access level password updates.

4.Keyfile contains access level passwords: keyfile is rejected.

- Multiple updates to access-level passwords via keyfile are permitted only when the one-time operation constraint is disabled,

                        and the ECU supports security features(signature or decryption).

- Note : Even after the one-time operation has been enabled, access level passwords can still be updated

      1:via UDS service 0xBE: [Security change password in CB-ME](security-change-password-in-cb.html "Security-Change-Password-in-CB"){.topiclink}.

      2:via C-API: [bds_sec_saveSecret](bds_sec_savesecret.html "bds_sec_saveSecret"){.topiclink}.        

oDigital Signature Requirements

§Digital signatures are critical for authenticating the origin and integrity of \`keyfile.hex\` updates:

- Initial Root Key/Certificate Injection: When a \`keyfile.hex\` contains the initial root key or certificate for injection, it must be signed by a user key that corresponds to the root key contained within that same \`keyfile.hex\`. This mechanism ensures that only authorized software development personnel, possessing the correct user key, can enable the signature check functionality on the device. It also mandates that the PC-side tooling for signing software is correctly configured before such critical \`keyfile.hex\` files can be generated.

- Mandatory Signature Check: Once the signature check functionality has been enabled on the RC (typically after the initial root key/certificate injection), all subsequent \`keyfile.hex\` updates must be digitally signed and successfully verified by the RC. Unsigned \`keyfile.hex\` files will be rejected.

oDigital Signature Hierarchy

§The digital signature scheme employs a two-tier hierarchy:

- Root Keys/Certificates: These form the top layer of trust. They are used to sign User Keys/Certificates.

- User Keys/Certificates:These intermediate keys are used to sign the hash of the actual data payloads (e.g., software binaries, \`keyfile.hex\`, \`unlockFile.hex\`).

§The trust chain can be visualized as:

- Root (e.g., PKI) → User (e.g., TPM) → Data (SW/keyfile/unlockFile)

oPackaging for Flashing

§For manufacturing and deployment convenience, \`keyfile.hex\` files can be concatenated with other software images: \`keyfile.hex\` can be appended to either the \`CB-ME.hex\` (bootloader image) or \`ASW.hex\` (application software image) for unified flashing in production environments (e.g., Bosch Rexroth site / OEM facility).

## keyfile Encrypted Data Field Format (ENCR) Documentation {#keyfile-encrypted-data-field-format-encr-documentation .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

This section details the structure and processing of the Encrypted Data Field (ENCR) within a keyfile. The primary purpose of this encrypted field is to ensure the confidentiality of sensitive information, such as passwords and secret keys, during their transport to the RC.

General Specifications and Requirements

- Integer Field Encoding: All integer fields within the decrypted data is coded in Big-Endian format. This means the Most Significant Byte (MSByte) is always placed first, regardless of the target architecture\'s native byte ordering. This standardization ensures consistent interpretation across different systems.

- Decryption Key Availability:

oFor CB-ME to successfully decrypt the keyfile, the necessary decryption key must be available to the CB-ME. The decryption key is hardcoded within the HSM (Hardware Security Module) firmware of RC40.

oOnce an AES decryption key is provisioned into RC40, the system will strictly only accept encrypted HEX files for flashing. Attempts to flash unencrypted HEX files will be rejected to maintain data confidentiality and integrity.

- Asymmetric Cryptography for Key File Generation: To prevent the sensitive decryption key from ever being present on the PC tool used to generate the keyfile, asymmetric cryptography is employed.

oThe keyfile generation tool uses a public key to encrypt the sensitive data.

oThe RC40 holds the corresponding private key, which is never exposed externally.

oThis design ensures that even if the PC tool is compromised, the private decryption key remains secure within the RC.

- In case the encryption padding (RSAES-OAEP-2048 padding with SHA256 and MGF1-SHA256) is found to be invalid during decryption process, the keyfile is rejected

- In case the length of the decrypted data does not match the expected size, the keyfile is rejected

- Algorithm:

oThe RC40 uses RSAES-OAEP-2048 with main hash = SHA256 and MGF1 = SHA256 to decrypt the Key-File-Encrypted-Data (KFED) into RAM

oOn RC40 the keys can be injected to HSM and then be cleared from RAM again
